The realm of the Sui dynasty, which reunited China in 589 after almost three centuries of division and ruled until 618. The map shows it in 600, and keeps the label in 700, by which time the Tang ruled.

Yang Jian, a general of mixed Chinese and Xianbei family, took the throne of the Northern Zhou in 581 and conquered the southern Chen in 589. He rebuilt Chang'an as a great planned capital, brought in one law code and coinage, and began choosing officials by written test, the root of the imperial examination.

His son Emperor Yang linked north and south with the Grand Canal, which carried southern grain north for over a thousand years. He also launched huge invasions of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo between 612 and 614, all of which failed. Their cost in men and labour set off revolts across the empire. Yang was murdered in 618, and his general Li Yuan founded the Tang, which kept most of the Sui's institutions.
